sourceRoute: Per city: the governing instrument was located from the city's own site first (ordinances page, then code publication), and the dimensional text was read on the most readable authoritative route available. Three routes were needed: (a) server-rendered ordinance text (Hewitt's Municode Appendix A page, West's and Beverly Hills' eCode360 codification, Riesel's own PDF); (b) rendered third-party mirrors of the city's own codified ordinance on Zoneomics where the authoritative route returns a JavaScript shell (Robinson, Bellmead, Woodway, Moody) -- each such read is declared in the table note and in the entries below, together with the authoritative source that failed; (c) plain HTTP anchor-text extraction where a page's labels carry the document links but a markdown render drops the hrefs (Riesel's development page). Every value's provenance names the route; where the authoritative source could not be read, the entry says so. No value in any table comes from a source I could not fetch: the one case where only a search-engine rendering of the authoritative document was legible (Bruceville-Eddy's eCode360 codification) produced no table and is reported as blocked.

entries.note: DECLINED, category 3, with one important finding recorded rather than coded: Gholson's code DOES state a real, readable setback rule -- Sec. 3.01.002 'Building setback lines' -- 'The minimum building setback lines shall be twenty-five (25) feet in front, fifteen (15) feet in the rear and ten (10) feet on each side, provided that on a corner lot the side yard on the street side of the lot shall be not less than twenty-five (25) feet. Variances may be granted when justified by the city council.' That is a genuine dimensional standard but it is NOT a district table: it is one city-wide building line, the code establishes no zoning districts, and the census carries no district stamp for these parcels (zoningRefused 840). The table shape and the router are district-keyed, so a row here would be unreachable and would invent a district that does not exist -- the failure mode this program hunts. Recorded instead, and raised as openThread 1 because the shape decision (does the program want jurisdiction-wide rows?) belongs to the planner, not to me. What would change it: a decision to carry jurisdiction-wide setback rules, at which point this is the first candidate, or the city adopting a zoning ordinance.

What would change it: the separate Zoning Ordinance document from City Hall (its adoption year would also settle what is in force), or the city publishing it. This is the one city in the lane where a public-records request is the acquisition path rather than a browser render.

Categories are scope rev 4 section 2b's: 1 = zoned with a staged layer; 2 = zoned without a staged layer (sub-case 2a queryable endpoint / 2b PDF-or-document-only map noted where determined); 3 = genuinely unzoned, declared on evidence of absence with the searches named.

openThreads: Gholson: the city's code states a real, readable city-wide setback rule (Sec. 3.01.002: 25 ft front / 15 ft rear / 10 ft each side, 25 ft on the corner street side) with NO district structure, and the census holds no district stamp for its 840 parcels. The district-keyed table shape and the router cannot carry it, so it is not coded. PROGRAM-LEVEL QUESTION for the planner, not for a lane: does the corpus want jurisdiction-wide rows (a shape decision), and if so is Gholson the first candidate? This is the only place in lane-d where a genuine dimensional standard was read and deliberately not written, so it should not be silently dropped.

Riesel: the nonresidential half of the same Appendix 1 (C-1, C-2, I-1, I-2, CBRD) is uncoded because the PDF text route collapses its rows (more tokens than columns) and its footnote letters collide with the residential table's. A rendered read of the same PDF, or the city's own Word/print original, would make 5 more rows available. The residential 8 are already in both repos.

Riesel vintage: the ordinance in force is No. 2026-04, which REPEALS Ordinance 2026-02 and adopts a new comprehensive zoning ordinance and map; no adoption or effective date is printed in the document as read (only the 2026-06-16 public-hearing date). Any Riesel row authored before this instrument describes a retired scheme -- worth a program-level note, since 'recently rezoned' is the vintage trap batch 1 flagged and this is a 2026 example.

Hewitt and Bellmead: scope rev 4 section 2b's teardown sample records 'Hewitt, Bellmead and Jarrell with layers', but the census/worklist rows for BOTH carry withDistrictOnRecord 0 and zoningRefused = every parcel. One of the two is wrong, and it changes the classification (category 1 vs 2). A staged-layer probe on these two is cheap and settles it; I did not have the census-side instrument to run it.

Robinson is the only row of the 19 with a district stamp on record (5,686 of 5,728 parcels) and a known layer endpoint (services7.arcgis.com/Ls5quuABi3I5K4Lg/arcgis/rest/services/Zoning_2024/FeatureServer/21, per the county contract's roster read), yet the contract's city.zoning_layer_staged is 'unaccounted'. If it is staged, the 14 rows I added become reachable for 5,686 parcels; if not, the table sits unreachable and the parcels stay refused. Staging probe requested.

Municode is NOT uniformly a JavaScript shell: it served Hewitt's entire Appendix A as server-rendered text to a plain fetch on this pass while returning a shell for Robinson, Bellmead and Woodway (and Lorena, Lacy-Lakeview). Any lane or planner rule that generalises 'Municode is unreadable' from batch 1 would over-declare. Recommend the route be probed per city and the result recorded, as done here.

The lane's tables are in legacy-design-tools; V4's PUD scan reads them from the shared clone P:/seat-worktrees/p258-setback-campaign/ldt-base via origin/seat/p258-lane-d, and 2026-09-16_p258_addedrows.mjs has LANES = [lane-a, lane-b, lane-c]. Without lane-d added to that list the scan never sees these 58 added rows. I did not edit the planner's script; I fetched origin/seat/p258-lane-d into the shared clone so the ref exists when the planner adds the lane (a fetch only -- no branch, no working tree and no lane branch was touched). Flagged so the operator can see the one mutation I made outside my own worktrees and revert it if the clone is pinned.

Bruceville-Eddy: the city's open-data page links a GIS map and a zoning map, so a queryable layer may exist even though the ordinance is walled. A staging/endpoint probe should run before anyone defaults this city to category 2b; if a layer exists, its district codes still need the walled Exhibit 14A text, so the block is real either way.

Route class to watch, from this lane: for 5 of the 8 acquired cities the values come from a rendered read of a live third-party mirror (Zoneomics) because the city's own publication (Municode) returns a shell; for 3 of them the city's own publication was readable (Hewitt via Municode, West and Beverly Hills via eCode360, Riesel via its own PDF -- note Beverly Hills needed a mirror for its height part only). A citation only a browser can produce is a defect; a mirror read is not that, but it is weaker than a city-product read. The planner may want a per-table field that says which it was, so a future re-verification knows what to re-fetch first. Every table note in this lane states it in prose in the meantime.

Ordinance defects recorded but not resolved (each could be its own small task if the program cares): Hewitt R-1-G's 'Maximum lot coverage' heading contains only a minimum-dwelling-size rule; Beverly Hills names its residential district 'R' in Part 1 and 'R-1 and R-2' in Parts 2/5/6 with no R-2 section anywhere; Moody's Article 3 headings (B1, HC) disagree with the table printed under Section 18 (GC) and with Article 1's list, and an AG district appears in no list; West's and Moody's side yards are adjacency- or use-keyed. In each case the table codes the printed scheme and quotes the mismatch rather than choosing a winner.

Crawford is the weakest decline in this lane and should be re-run cheaply: the city's ordinances page served no content to a plain fetch, so the ordinance list was never enumerated. That is an unchecked absence, not a checked one, and the entry says so. A browser render of crawfordtx.gov/ordinances would close it.

Leroy's Le Roy, Illinois false positive is worth a program-level note if other lanes cover small Texas towns with name collisions: the top search result for 'City of Leroy building permit handbook' is another state's zoning ordinance, printed with the same city name.
